problem_statement: A node configured to allow more than one IPv6 address to be associated with a single link-layer neighbor can only retain one such address. When a neighbor is reachable over a link that owns both a link-local address (fe80::202:2:2:2) and a unique-local address (fd00::202:2:2:2), the node successfully answers a ping to one of them but fails to answer the ping to the other, and the neighbor-cache inspection reports only a single IPv6 address bound to the neighbor's link-layer address (0002.0002.0002.0002) instead of both. The required behavior is that, when the multi-address capability is enabled, both the link-local and the unique-local address of the same neighbor are cached against the same link-layer address, both remain reachable (state Reachable), and a neighbor-cache query lists the two IPv6 addresses side by side for that single link-layer neighbor.
causal_chain: The two failing scenarios build the mote with the multi-IPv6-address neighbor capability enabled and drive it through a script that pings the neighbor's link-local address, then its unique-local address, then issues the neighbor-cache query, asserting that both IPv6 addresses appear for the one link-layer address in the Reachable state. Before the production change the neighbor cache keys entries strictly by link-layer address and holds at most one IPv6 address per link-layer neighbor, so the second address cannot be represented/resolved and the assertion that two IPv6 addresses are associated with the same link-layer address cannot be satisfied; the single-address ping scenarios (the pass-to-pass set) exercise only one address per neighbor and are unaffected.

verification.reason: The statement describes the desired observable behavior but omits the exact configuration names and several public API/behavior details required by the hidden tests; these can be added without dictating the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden tests enable and use the configuration option UIP_DS6_NBR_CONF_MULTI_IPV6_ADDRS and the macro UIP_DS6_NBR_MAX_6ADDRS_PER_NBR, but the statement does not name them.

The hidden tests check public neighbor-cache behavior not stated by the problem: uip_ds6_nbr_add must fail when the per-link-layer or overall cache limit is reached, uip_ds6_nbr_num must count cached IPv6 addresses, head/next must iterate all entries, lladdr_from_ipaddr must resolve the link-layer address, and uip_ds6_nbr_rm must remove an entry and return 1.

The Cooja test expects the ip-nbr output for the described neighbor to list the link-local address before the unique-local address and to show state Reachable, but the original statement does not specify the order.

The hidden test configurations use build settings such as WITH_NBR_MULTI_IPV6_ADDRS=1 to select the feature, and the statement does not state the public configuration name or that the capability may be enabled through it.

problem_statement_fixed:
A node configured to allow more than one IPv6 address to be associated with a single link-layer neighbor can only retain one such address. When a neighbor is reachable over a link that owns both a link-local address (fe80::202:2:2:2) and a unique-local address (fd00::202:2:2:2), the node successfully answers a ping to one of them but fails to answer the ping to the other, and the neighbor-cache inspection reports only a single IPv6 address bound to the neighbor's link-layer address (0002.0002.0002.0002) instead of both. The required behavior is that, when the multi-address capability is enabled, both the link-local and the unique-local address of the same neighbor are cached against the same link-layer address, both remain reachable (state Reachable), and a neighbor-cache query lists the two IPv6 addresses side by side for that single link-layer neighbor.

The multi-address capability must be enabled by defining UIP_DS6_NBR_CONF_MULTI_IPV6_ADDRS to 1; a build variable such as WITH_NBR_MULTI_IPV6_ADDRS=1 may be used to define this option. When the capability is enabled, UIP_DS6_NBR_MAX_6ADDRS_PER_NBR must define the maximum number of IPv6 addresses that may be associated with one link-layer address, and it must be large enough to accommodate the link-local and unique-local addresses described above. When the capability is disabled, the existing single-IPv6-address-per-link-layer behavior is retained.

For the multi-address case, the neighbor-cache API must expose the following behavior: uip_ds6_nbr_add() must return a valid uip_ds6_nbr_t for each IPv6 address that can be cached, and NULL if the per-link-layer limit, UIP_DS6_NBR_MAX_6ADDRS_PER_NBR, is reached or the overall limit of NBR_TABLE_MAX_NEIGHBORS distinct link-layer addresses is reached. The returned entry must contain the IPv6 address and state passed to uip_ds6_nbr_add(). uip_ds6_nbr_num() must return the number of cached IPv6 addresses. uip_ds6_nbr_head() and uip_ds6_nbr_next() must iterate over all cached IPv6 addresses. uip_ds6_nbr_lladdr_from_ipaddr() and uip_ds6_nbr_ll_lookup() must resolve the associated link-layer address. uip_ds6_nbr_rm() must remove a cached IPv6 address and return 1 on success; after all IPv6 addresses associated with a link-layer address have been removed, that link-layer address must no longer be present in the neighbor cache.

A neighbor-cache query for the described neighbor must show both IPv6 addresses as separate entries for the same link-layer address, with the link-local address entry before the unique-local address entry, and each entry must show state Reachable. The node must answer pings to both addresses in the multi-address case, and the fix must not regress the ability to answer pings to both addresses in configurations where the multi-address capability is not enabled.
